unit.can_do_en: introduce myself at work and ask where things are.

brief.situation_en: Maria asks Hanna about her week.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Hanna, mihin aikaan mun työpäivä alkaa?
lines.text_kirja: Hanna, mihin aikaan minun työpäiväni alkaa?
lines.gloss_en: Hanna, what time does my working day start?

judge.reason: Only register differences (mun/minun, työpäiväni possessive); same question about start time.

lines.speaker: Hanna
lines.gloss_en: At eight. And it ends at four.

judge.reason: Kaheksalta is the spoken form of kahdeksalta; same times (eight, four).

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Do I work on Saturdays too?

judge.reason: Teenks mä/Teenkö minä: same question about working on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Hanna
lines.text_puhe: Et. Sä teet töitä maanantaist perjantaihin.
lines.text_kirja: Et. Sinä teet töitä maanantaista perjantaihin.
lines.gloss_en: No. You work Monday to Friday.

judge.reason: Same negation and same days, Monday to Friday; only register differs.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Good. Can I work from home?

judge.reason: Voinks mä tehä/Voinko minä tehdä: same question about remote work.
Joo and kyllä both mean yes; perjantaisin is the same.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Nice! Where do I get a key card?

judge.reason: Mist mä/Mistä minä: same question about where to get the key card.

lines.speaker: Hanna
lines.gloss_en: From the lobby. I'll come with you.

judge.reason: Mä tuun sun kaa = Minä tulen sinun kanssasi; same meaning, 'I'll come with you'.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for my

forms.why_en: This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
And: joins the coffee and the bun in the order.
'It.' Nominative singular, referring back to the price.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 1st person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö

forms.why_en: Means 'also' or 'too': coffee as well as oat milk.
Means 'good!' or 'great!', showing you are happy.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 1st person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö

forms.why_en: Yes. In everyday speech people often say joo instead.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Means 'from where?'; the elative ending -stä means 'from'. Spoken: 'mist'.
